content: 1. Flucytosine increases the levels of tenofovir DF by reducing renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and flurbiprofen can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Toxicity may occur when tenofovir DF is co-administered with other drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, such as high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 4. Fosphenytoin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Foscarnet and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Fostamatinib may increase the concentrations of BCRP substrate drugs. Monitor for toxicities of BCRP substrates, and dosage reduction may be required when co-administered. 8. Ganciclovir increases the levels of tenofovir DF through mechanisms involving renal function reduction or competition for active tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Gentamicin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Gentamicin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Monitor for toxicities. 12. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and ibuprofen can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Indinavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and indomethacin can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 17. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and ketoprofen can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and ketorolac can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Lamivudine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for adverse reactions if co-administered with P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Reduce P-gp substrate dose if needed. 23. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and meclofenamate can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and mefenamic acid can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and meloxicam can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of memantine by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Potential for increased toxicity. 28. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of metformin by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased risk of lactic acidosis. 29. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of midodrine by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Potential for increased toxicity. 30. Mitomycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Mitomycin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of morphine by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Potential for increased toxicity. 32. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and nabumetone can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and naproxen can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Nelfinavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Neomycin PO and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Neomycin PO increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Nevirapine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting GI absorption. Applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if increased HIV viral load is confirmed. 38. Oxaliplatin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination may also increase tenofovir levels. 39. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and oxaprozin can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Pamidronate increases the levels of tenofovir DF by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. 41. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and pemetrexed can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Penicillamine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Penicillamine increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Pentamidine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination may also increase tenofovir levels. 44. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of peramivir by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. 45. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and piroxicam can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 46. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of pramipexole by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Potential for increased toxicity. 47. Probenecid increases the levels of tenofovir DF by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Potential for increased toxicity. 48. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of procainamide by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Potential for increased toxicity. 49. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and quinidine can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by likely inhibiting BCRP (ABCG2) transport. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Ritonavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor BCRP substrates for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 53. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 54. Sirolimus and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Sirolimus increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and sitagliptin can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for tenofovir-associated adverse reactions in patients receiving EPCLUSA concomitantly with a regimen containing tenofovir DF. 58. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 59. Stiripentol is a BCRP transport inhibitor. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects are experienced when co-administered. 60. Streptomycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Streptomycin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and sulindac can lead to mutual increases in drug levels due to decreased renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 62. Tacrolimus and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 63. Tafamidis increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting breast cancer resistant protein (BCRP) in vitro. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Tafamidis meglumine increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting breast cancer resistant protein (BCRP) in vitro. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Telavancin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Telavancin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Tipranavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Tobramycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Tobramycin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely.
